reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Rejection of international AI control
themes.definition: Explicit rejection of international or 'globalist' schemes to govern or control AI, preferring national oversight.
themes.inclusion: Include passages rejecting multilateral AI governance or control frameworks.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages calling for international AI rules (AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE).
themes.boundary_cases: Statements that national law enforcement will oversee AI instead of international bodies also fit here.

examples.quote: The United States also totally rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control for the artificial intelligence

themes.label: Winning the AI race for dominance
themes.definition: AI framed as a strategic race where whoever leads wins, with emphasis on national lead over rivals and not stifling growth.
themes.inclusion: Include passages claiming national AI leadership over rivals or that winning AI determines power.
themes.exclusion: Exclude national AI programs described without competitive framing (use AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY).
themes.boundary_cases: Claims of leading 'safely and responsibly' while encouraging AI growth fit here.

examples.quote: whoever wins SI, whoever wins super intelligent, wins. That's the group that wins. And we're leading now over China by a lot
We're going to encourage it, not rein it in.

themes.label: Dismissal of AI doom warnings
themes.definition: Speaker dismisses warnings of catastrophic AI risk as alarmism, while acknowledging some challenges.
themes.inclusion: Include passages ridiculing or rejecting claims that AI poses existential or catastrophic risk.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages that affirm catastrophic AI risk (AI_SAFETY_EXISTENTIAL).
themes.boundary_cases: A passing 'we have to be careful' alongside dismissal of doom still fits here.

examples.quote: These are the same people that are now saying that AI is going to kill us all, that robots are going to attack us

themes.label: AI for weapons treaty verification
themes.definition: AI proposed as a tool to verify compliance with arms control treaties such as the Biological Weapons Convention.
themes.inclusion: Include proposals to use AI for verification or enforcement of disarmament regimes.
themes.boundary_cases: If the UN is invited to host the effort, also code AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: by pioneering an AI verification system that everyone can trust

themes.label: AI could be great or dangerous
themes.definition: AI described as potentially one of the great things ever but also dangerous.
themes.inclusion: Include explicit framings of AI as both beneficial and dangerous.
themes.boundary_cases: Brief asides within other topics still count if both sides are explicit.

examples.quote: it could be one of the great things ever, but it also can be dangerous, but it could be put to tremendous use and tremendous good

value.rationale: US passages reject international AI control, frame AI ('superintelligence') as a race to win while dismissing doom warnings; the 2025 passage instead proposes an AI verification system for the BWC and notes AI's dual potential.
